graph.question: Before committing a GPU screening run: does cubic boron arsenide actually conduct heat at ~1300 W/mK at 300 K?

claims.text: Ab-initio theory (Lindsay, Broido & Reinecke, PRL 2013) predicts κ ≈ 2200 W/mK for defect-free cubic BAs at room temperature.
State-of-the-art cubic BAs crystals show a measured room-temperature thermal conductivity of ~1300 W/mK.
Early BAs crystals measured only ~200 W/mK, an order of magnitude below theory, because of defects (Lv et al., APL 2015).
Three independent groups reported κ ≈ 1000–1300 W/mK in Science in 2018 (Kang et al.; Li et al.; Tian et al.).
Including four-phonon scattering lowers the theoretical ceiling from ~2200 to ~1400 W/mK (Feng, Lindsay & Ruan, PRB 2017).
Point defects (arsenic vacancies, antisite pairs) are the dominant κ limiters in real BAs crystals.
At ~1300 W/mK, BAs would outperform copper roughly 3× as a passive heat spreader for electronics cooling.
Cubic BAs is commercially available as wafer-scale substrates for thermal-management applications.
BAs synthesis remains limited to small (mm-scale) single crystals grown by chemical vapor transport.

graph.question: Is the thermal conductivity of cubic boron arsenide really ~1300 W/mK at room temperature?

claims.text: Three-phonon scattering ab initio calculations in 2013 predicted cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) has a room-temperature thermal conductivity exceeding 2000 W/mK.
Including four-phonon scattering in 2017–2018 ab initio models reduced the predicted room-temperature thermal conductivity of pristine c-BAs to approximately 1250–1400 W/mK.
In 2018, Kang et al. measured a room-temperature thermal conductivity of ~1300 W/mK in defect-free regions of c-BAs using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR).
Simultaneous 2018 TDTR studies by Li et al. and Tian et al. measured room-temperature c-BAs thermal conductivity peaking at ~1000–1160 W/mK rather than 1300 W/mK.
Point defects, arsenic vacancies, and carbon or silicon impurities in chemical-vapor-transport grown c-BAs suppress bulk thermal conductivity below 1300 W/mK Across millimeter scales.
TDTR spot sizes of 5–10 micrometers and high modulation frequencies suffer from ballistic phonon transport artifacts that complicate extracting intrinsic bulk thermal conductivity in c-BAs.
Subsequent 2022–2023 experimental studies measuring high-mobility c-BAs confirmed local room-temperature thermal conductivities reaching 1200–1300 W/mK.
Cubic boron arsenide simultaneously exhibits ambipolar carrier mobility above 1500 cm²/Vs and thermal conductivity over 1200 W/mK at 300 K, outperforming silicon for electronics cooling.
Commercial wafer-scale synthesis of defect-free c-BAs remains unachieved as of 2024 due to sub-millimeter crystal growth limits in chemical vapor transport.

graph.question: Is an air fryer really cheaper to run than an electric oven?

claims.text: A typical air fryer uses ~0.4-0.5 kWh per use, versus ~1.0-1.5 kWh for a full-size electric oven cooking a comparable meal.
Running an air fryer costs about 10p per typical use, versus about 35p for an electric oven at 2025 UK electricity prices.
Air fryers preheat in 2-3 minutes versus 10-15 minutes for an electric oven, cutting total cooking time for most dishes.
Which? 2024 testing found air fryers cheaper than an electric oven for small portions such as chips, chicken and roast vegetables.
Typical UK electricity costs about 24.5p per kWh under the 2025 price cap, the unit rate behind both appliance estimates.
An air fryer basket holds roughly 3-6 litres, so family-sized meals need several rounds where one oven cycle cooks everything at once.
A household swapping four oven sessions a week for the air fryer saves roughly £50 a year on electricity.
Air fryers are always healthier than cooking the same food in an oven.
The 'healthier' marketing line rests on using less oil than deep frying — it says nothing about running cost.

graph.question: Is my landlord right that the mould in my flat is harmless condensation?

claims.text: The 2009 WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality state that no safe minimum threshold exists for indoor mould exposure, linking all dampness-related mould to elevated respiratory risks.

Common condensation-fed indoor fungi like Cladosporium, Penicillium, and Aspergillus release allergens, beta-glucans, and VOCs that trigger asthma exacerbations and rhinitis even in non-atopic adults.
The 2020 Rochdale coronal inquest into the death of two-year-old Awaab Ishak ruled that prolonged exposure to household condensation mould caused fatal acute airway oedema.
Under BS 5250:2021, indoor mould germinates when surface relative humidity exceeds 80% for prolonged periods, typically caused by thermal bridging or inadequate mechanical extract ventilation.
Approved Document F (2021 edition) of the UK Building Regulations mandates continuous extract rates of at least 15 L/s in bathrooms and 30 L/s in kitchens to prevent condensation.
The Housing Ombudsman's October 2021 Spotlight Report on Damp and Mould instructed UK landlords to stop attributing condensation to tenant 'lifestyle' where structural or ventilation defects exist.
The Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018 makes UK landlords legally liable for severe condensation damp and mould under the Housing Health and Safety Rating System (HHSRS).
Under the Social Housing (Regulation) Act 2023 (Awaab's Law), UK social landlords must investigate reported damp and mould hazards within 14 calendar days.
The global commercial market for smart indoor air quality and humidity sensors exceeded $4.5 billion in 2023 due to rising residential demand for automated mould prevention.

graph.question: Is it safe to charge an e-bike battery indoors overnight?

claims.text: UK e-bike and e-scooter battery fires rose sharply: London Fire Brigade attended one roughly every two days in 2023/24.
Charging a certified (UL/EN 50604) e-bike battery indoors is safe.
Most e-bike battery fires involve damaged, aftermarket or mismatched chargers and packs, not certified originals.
Once a lithium battery enters thermal runaway it cannot be extinguished by normal domestic means, and the vented vapour cloud can ignite in seconds.
UK regulation lags the risk: there is no mandatory third-party certification for e-bike conversion kits at the point of sale.
Charging in hallways or exits puts the fire between you and the only escape route — the main factor in fatal e-bike fires.
Insurers increasingly exclude or void claims where an uncertified e-bike battery was charged indoors.
E-bike batteries explode spontaneously even when they are not charging.
The safe-practice consensus: charge while awake and present, use the original charger, keep the battery away from exits, and stop at any sign of damage or heat.
